text:
lee_support: FYI customer acme-inc on Dedicated EU is seeing intermittent 500s + big tail latency on /v1/generate. Reported window 2026-03-15 10:12-10:18 UTC. Sample request IDs: req_8a9f3c, req_8a9f40. They also reported a node reboot/gpu OOM around 10:14 UTC. Need checklist for log + metrics collection so we can reproduce and hand to infra/SRE.

alex_sre: Thanks — can you post the tenant id, exact pods that served those requests (if known), and a minimal curl repro? Also we should grab node-level dmesg and nv-smi around 10:14.

lee_support: Tenant: tenant-acme-42. Pod list from the customer UI looks like runtime/gateway + model pods. Time window again ~10:12-10:18 UTC. Minimal curl I asked them to run:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello world","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://dedicated-eu.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b
```
They said the failing request id returned 500 and the response body was just `{"error":"internal"}`.

maria_eng: OK — step checklist for collection: 
1) kubectl get pods -n tenant-acme-42 --show-labels > pods.txt
2) kubectl logs <gateway-pod> -c gateway --since=30m > gateway.log
3) kubectl logs <runtime-pod> -c runtime --since=30m > runtime.log
4) kubectl describe pod <runtime-pod> > pod_desc.txt
5) on the node: sudo dmesg --ctime | sed -n '1,300p' > dmesg.txt
6) sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 500 > kern_tail.txt
7) nvidia-smi -q -x > nv-smi.xml
8) collect gpu metrics from prom endpoint: curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep -E 'nvidia|gpu' > gpu_metrics.txt
Please replace angle brackets with actual names; keep original timestamps.

alex_sre: Also run these commands if you can: 
```bash
# collect kubectl logs for replicaset of model
kubectl get pods -n tenant-acme-42 -l app=redwood-model -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl logs {} -n tenant-acme-42 --since=30m > model_pods.log
# node-level snapshot
ssh root@gpu-eu-07 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-15 10:00" --until "2026-03-15 10:30"' > kubelet_journal.txt
```
If you have a failing request id, grep logs for that `req_8a9f3c`.

sana_support: When you have the files, create a debug bundle so SRE can ingest quickly:
```bash
# using our helper tool
rwc-bundle collect --tenant tenant-acme-42 --since "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z" --until "2026-03-15T10:30:00Z" -o /tmp/tenant-acme-42-bundle.tar.gz
# fallback: manual tar
tar czf /tmp/tenant-acme-42-manual.tar.gz pods.txt gateway.log runtime.log model_pods.log pod_desc.txt dmesg.txt kern_tail.txt nv-smi.xml gpu_metrics.txt kubelet_journal.txt
```
Upload link (internal): https://internal-files.redwood.example/upload (include ticket id in upload). If you want I can generate a pre-signed one-off.

ops-bot: debug-bundle-helper v2.4 started collection for tenant-acme-42 (job id dbg-20260315-01). ETA ~40s.

lee_support: quick note from customer logs they pasted: kernel logged `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` around 10:14 and runtime process segfaulted shortly after. snippet: 
```
[Mar15 10:14:22] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
I'll attach the raw logs once bundle is ready.

maria_eng: Xid 79 usually indicates GPU driver/firmware or hardware reset. For a repro please also capture: 
- `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -lms 1000` for 30s during repro
- `rdma-smi` if present
- `kubectl top pods -n tenant-acme-42 --containers` pre/failure snapshots
Also, add header `x-redwood-trace: 1` to curl to force request traces into the gateway logs. Example: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" -H "x-redwood-trace: 1" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://dedicated-eu.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt
```
This yields tcp-level trace + request id mapping.

alex_sre: When you upload the bundle, include a tiny reproduce.sh that hits the same model with same payloads and the two failing request ids in an env var so we can replay against staging. Also include the exact image tags from `kubectl get pods -o wide` so we can consult build artifacts. Assigning SRE oncall to this: @alex_sre (me) will own for now. P1 until we confirm isolated cluster issue.

lee_support: Understood. I'll run the collector and ask customer to run the curl with `x-redwood-trace`. I'll push the bundle to internal upload and paste link here once done.

alex_sre: :thumbsup: please paste the bundle URL + the single-line `kubectl get pods -n tenant-acme-42 -o wide` output. If the NV link shows repeated Xid 79 we will escalate to infra and OEM.

sana_support: I generated a presigned upload: https://internal-files.redwood.example/signed/abc123 (expires in 24h). Please use that and add ticket #SUP-4621 in the metadata.

lee_support: bundle uploaded to that signed url, filename tenant-acme-42-bundle.tar.gz, ticket SUP-4621. kubectl get pods -o wide output pasted below: 
```
NAME                                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE        NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
gateway-5b7d9c7d8d-ptx4w           1/1     Running   0          2d    10.42.3.15   gpu-eu-07   <none>           <none>
model-redwood-13b-0                 1/1     Running   3          7d    10.42.4.11   gpu-eu-09   <none>           <none>
runtime-8c9f7d6b-2lqk1             0/1     CrashLoopBackOff 6    3h    10.42.5.22   gpu-eu-07   <none>           <none>
```
I'll mark the ticket with P1 and assign to SRE-oncall.

alex_sre: Received bundle, starting ingest. Pulling nv-smi and dmesg now. Will update with a short triage in ~30m.

maria_eng: If we can't repro locally, ask customer to try a short stress test hitting the same model with small payloads and `x-redwood-trace` header so we get timing correlation.

lee_support: will do. thanks all.
